problem: Prior VLN agents (Seq2Seq/attention, Speaker-Follower, EnvDrop, etc.) learn to understand each instruction from scratch on small task-specific data. They do not reuse vision-grounded prior knowledge. The closest pre-training work (PreSS) plugs in an off-the-shelf text-only BERT and only targets R2R. Generic VLP models (ViLBERT/LXMERT) need Faster R-CNN region features, which is infeasible for 36-view panoramas and ignores actions.
motivation: Instructions only loosely and partially describe the trajectory, so they are ambiguous unless grounded in visual states. Objects in instructions and views share common forms and relations that could be learned once as a joint representation and transferred. VLN training data is small (R2R has about 104K image-text-action triplets), so self-supervised pre-training on synthesized data should improve generalization to unseen environments and to new VLN tasks.
key_idea: Pre-train an LXMERT-style vision-language Transformer from scratch on about 6.5M image-text-action triplets (R2R plus speaker-synthesized instructions) with image-attended masked language modeling and single-step action prediction, then use its visually grounded contextual word embeddings as a drop-in instruction encoder for existing VLN agents (R2R, CVDN, HANNA).
insight: Pre-training that grounds language in panoramic views and actions transfers better than text-only pre-training. On HANNA test unseen, SR is 52.91 with MLM+AP vs 44.29 with MLM only (Table 6, appendix HANNA ablation), and 24.12/26.36 with BERT feature-based/fine-tuned. On CVDN, GP (Mixed, All) is 3.15 vs 2.64 for BERT re-pre-trained on the same R2R text, although AP adds only 0.01 GP there (3.14 with MLM only). Only the language-stream outputs are used downstream, so the gain comes from visually grounded contextual word embeddings rather than a new policy. Pre-training also speeds early fine-tuning and narrows the seen/unseen gap: HANNA SPL gap is 30.66 vs 38.42 for ANNA, and the CVDN learning curves show a smaller gap than Seq2Seq. Fine-tuning the cross-attention layers after feature-based training (two-stage) gives a further gain over frozen features (R2R test unseen SPL 51 vs 49).
method: Input embeddings: each of the 36 panorama views is a 2048-d ResNet feature concatenated with a 128-d heading/elevation encoding (sin/cos repeated 32×), passed through FC + LayerNorm to d_h=768. Text uses standard Transformer token+position embeddings with LN.

Encoder (LXMERT-style, trained from scratch): single-modal Transformer encoders (9 text layers, 1 vision layer) followed by 3 cross-modal layers. Each cross layer has cross-attention to the other modality, then self-attention and an FFN. The last-layer output z serves as features.
Image-attended MLM: 15% of instruction words are replaced by [MASK] and predicted from the surrounding words plus attention over all panorama views, so word embeddings become visually grounded.

Action prediction (AP): an FC layer on the fused [CLS] output predicts the next navigable direction from the current panorama and the instruction alone, with no history; state-action pairs are treated as i.i.d. Total loss is L_MLM + L_AP. Masked image modeling was tried and did not help.

Pre-training data: 104K R2R train triplets plus 1,020K speaker-synthesized instructions (Speaker-Follower speaker) on shortest paths in training environments, i.e. 6,482K triplets (about 6,582K total). Trained on 8 V100s with AdamW, lr 5e-5, 20 epochs.

Downstream adaptation: the contextual word embeddings replace the instruction encoder input of existing agents. R2R uses the EnvDrop LSTM encoder-decoder (augmented listener schedule), then a two-stage step fine-tunes the cross-attention layers for 20k iterations at lr 2e-6. CVDN/NDH uses the same encoder-decoder with dialog history truncated to 300 tokens. HANNA uses the ANNA agent, whose assistant instructions are encoded with PREVALENT. Feature-based mode is the default.

setting.backbone: PREVALENT Transformer encoder (9 text / 1 vision / 3 cross layers, d=768; pre-trained from scratch) + ImageNet ResNet view features; downstream policies: EnvDrop LSTM encoder-decoder (R2R), NDH Seq2Seq-style LSTM (CVDN), ANNA agent (HANNA)

numbers_note: R2R SR/SPL are printed as integers in Table 1 and as fractions in Table 5 (converted to percent here). There is a small inconsistency: val-seen SPL is 65 in Table 1 but 0.66 for the same two-stage model in Table 5. The CVDN ablation (Table 4) does not state its split; its 'All' row matches the val-unseen numbers of Table 2. Table 4 also reports the full model with other dialog-input types, given as Oracle/Navigator/Mixed GP: Navigation QA 2.80/3.01/3.28 and Oracle Answer 2.78/3.44/3.38. Learning-curve comparisons (vs EnvDrop on R2R, vs Seq2Seq on CVDN) are only shown in Figure 4. BERT-baseline ablation rows are omitted as non-own methods.
results: On R2R test unseen, PREVALENT reaches SR 54 / SPL 51 in the single-instruction greedy setting, beating EnvDrop (51/47) and PreSS (49/45). In the multiple-instruction setting it reaches 59/56 vs PreSS 57/53. On CVDN it reaches GP (Mixed) 3.15 val-unseen and 2.44 test-unseen vs Seq2Seq 2.10/2.35, taking the top leaderboard position. On HANNA test unseen it gets SR 52.91 / SPL 28.72 / NE 5.29 vs ANNA 47.45/25.50/7.67. It is slightly worse than ANNA on seen environments and requests more help.
limitations: Pre-training uses a single panorama per step with no trajectory history (state-action pairs are treated as i.i.d.). Only the language-stream outputs are used downstream, so the policy itself is not pre-trained.
Pre-training data covers only R2R training scenes, and 98.4% of it is speaker-synthesized instructions (potentially noisy, low diversity). Masked image modeling did not help.
Gains are small in some settings: AP adds only about 0.01 GP on CVDN; HANNA seen-env SR/SPL drop vs ANNA and #R rises. Most results use frozen features (feature-based mode).
